questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest linting and security checks in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gating
- SecurityContext and imagePullPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-manifest-gate.yml
name: Manifest Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          set -e
          violations=0
          for f in $(git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -E '\\.ya?ml$' ); do
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].readinessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].livenessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsNonRoot' "$f" | grep -q true; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser' "$f" | grep -q '1000'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].imagePullPolicy' "$f" | grep -q 'Always'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
          done
          if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing.yaml (no readiness/liveness probes or runAsNonRoot)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

```yaml
# passing.yaml (probes present, non-root, Always)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this gate to cover initContainers?
- How would you surface violations to developers (e.g., PR checks, annotated reviews)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world security requires automated SBOMs and multi-tool vulnerability checks to prevent risky images from entering registries.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM generation with Syft
- Parallel scans with Trivy and Grype
- PR gating and artifact attachment
- Validation in CI and via PR comments

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions workflow (yaml)
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          docker build -t myimage:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock anchore/syft:latest DockerImage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Scan with Trivy
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock aquasecurity/trivy:latest image --exit-code 1 --no-progress myimage:${{ github.sha }} || true
      - name: Scan with Grype
        run: |
          grype myimage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > grype.json || true
      - name: Upload SBOMs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sboms
          path: sbom.json, grype.json
      - name: Fail if CVEs found
        run: |
          if [ -s grype.json ] && grep -q '"score": 7' grype.json; then exit 1; fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this gate for a multi-arch build?
- How would you integrate SBOM attestation into your registry metadata?

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: secure-pods
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: ensure-secure-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
        namespaces: [secure]
    validate:
      message: SecurityContext must be non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, no privileged, drop ALL
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: "*"
            securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
              runAsUser: 1000
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              capabilities:
                drop:
                - ALL
  - name: image-policy
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
        namespaces: [secure]
    validate:
      message: Image must come from allowed registry
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: example.com/secure/*
  - name: image-pull-policy
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
        namespaces: [secure]

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in policy-as-code across multi-cloud, multi-tenant ML infrastructure. It combines security hardening (image signing, secret management), resource governance (GPU quotas, container limits), network segmentation (default-deny policies), and operational reliability (canary deployments with SLO validation)—all critical for enterprise-grade ML platforms.

## Key Concepts

- **Policy Engines**: Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper provide declarative, Kubernetes-native admission control
- **Image Signing**: Cosign ensures container image integrity and provenance verification
- **Secret Management**: ExternalSecret/SecretStore enables secure, dynamic secret injection from external stores
- **Resource Quotas**: ResourceQuota and LimitRange enforce compute, memory, and GPU allocation per tenant
- **Network Policies**: Namespace-scoped default-deny with per-tenant allow rules implements zero-trust networking
- **Canary/SLO Integration**: Prometheus metrics validate deployment health before traffic shifting
- **CI Integration**: Automated policy testing and manifest validation ensure consistent enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy: require Cosign-signed images from approved registries
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: check-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*.gcr.io/tenant-*/**"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "*@company.com"
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests end-to-end security for ML artifacts, combining signing attestations, GitOps, and runtime policy in Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore Cosign sign-blob attest and verify-blob
- Model provenance and SBOM
- GitOps with Argo CD
- Admission policies: OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign a model blob and create an attestation
cosign sign-blob -key cosign.key models/model-v1.bin
cosign attest -key cosign.key --predicate predicate.json models/model-v1.bin
cosign verify-blob -key cosign.pub models/model-v1.bin
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy requiring attestation before deployment
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-model-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attested-model-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: Attestation required for model artifact
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations.cosign_attested: "true"
```

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign_attested"] == "true"
  msg = "Model artifact must be attested with cosign before deployment"
}
```
